notes:
Account overview: Verdigris is a fast-growing e-commerce personalization platform (catalog + realtime recommendations). Looking to offload inference ops to Redwood Dedicated to avoid capitalizing GPU fleet. Primary ask: firm throughput guarantees with clear concurrency caps and burst policy.

Recent timeline / activities:
- 2026-01-20: Intro call (AE Maya + SE Diego) — high level requirements, security checklist requested.
- 2026-01-28: Security deep-dive (FF ff-20260128-security-qna). Customer requires SOC2 + KMS + VPC peering, data residency in US only.
- 2026-02-10: Performance POC kickoff (FF ff-20260210-verdigris-poc). Completed synthetic stress test week of 2026-02-22.
- 2026-02-24: POC results review — Redwood baseline config (16xA100-equivalent reserved) achieved 32k sustained tokens/sec with 500 concurrent chat sessions; 95p latency per-request ~210ms.
- 2026-02-25: Customer pushed for higher guarantee; requested min 45k tokens/sec sustained and concurrency cap of 800 with bursts to 1,200 for shopping peaks (10-15 minute windows).
- 2026-02-26: Redwood proposed tiered guarantee: 30k guaranteed, optional +15k premium burst pool (burst billed separately) and concurrency cap 700; SLO credits tied to monthly availability and 95p latency.

Use-case / requirements summary (customer wording fragments):
- "Checkout personalization must never slow down; 95p token latency target <=250ms, ideally <200ms."
- Chat + personalization + reranking mixed workload: heavy small-turn chat (avg 60 tokens) + rerank for top-10 at ~200 qps during peaks.
- Throughput goals: target sustained 40k-45k tokens/sec during promotional windows; normal sustained 20-30k.
- Concurrency: expecting 500 steady concurrent chat sessions, want headroom to 800 for flash sales.
- Burst policy: 10–15 minute bursts to 1,000–1,200 concurrent sessions; willing to pay for burst capacity but wants predictable billing and caps on peak billing.
- Model preference: mix of open 34B quantized for cost + one higher-quality 70B variant for personalization experiments; expect Redwood to recommend quantization/packing and batching settings.

Throughput guarantee negotiation notes (tactical):
- Customer position: insists on min 45k tokens/sec guarantee across dedicated pool (not regionally partitioned). Wants concurrency cap >=800 and burst to 1,200 for up to 15 minutes with no throttling.
- Redwood position: proposes baseline guaranteed 30k tokens/sec (SLA-backed), optional burst pool (pre-warmed reserved GPUs) that can add up to +15k tokens/sec for scheduled events; concurrency cap 700 standard, 900 with burst pool.
- Pricing tension: customer wants credits for missed guarantee >=20% of monthly bill; Redwood prefers sliding credits with caps and requires clear definitions of "sustained" (5-minute sliding window vs 1-minute).
- Measurement: customer accepts token/sec and 95p latency metrics but requests ability to run third-party probes and a joint measurement report for disputed months.
- Deployment note: customer will require regional failover policy—need cross-region standby pool with automated routing; wants fallback to smaller model variant on overload.

Reserved GPU planning (notes):
- Customer internal ask: reserve equivalent of 16 A100-80GB in primary region + 6 GPU warm standby in secondary region.
- Redwood suggests alternative: 12 reserved + autoscale buffer (burst pool) sized and priced for 15-minute peaks; lower monthly commit, burst credits for consumption.
- Cost tradeoffs: customer calculates that moving to 20 reserved GPUs meets 45k sustained target but is above their budget ceiling; negotiating hybrid commit + burst is primary path.

Next steps / action items:
- AE Maya: update SOW to include two SLA options (flat guaranteed tokens/sec vs tiered guaranteed + burst) and modeling of monthly credit schedule. Due 2026-03-05.
- SE Diego: prepare deterministic test harness and joint measurement plan; include third-party probe agreement and thresholds.
- Legal: customer to send standard SLA redlines; Redwood to return redlines on credits/penalty caps.
- Schedule: procurement decision targeted 2026-04; need final pricing + SLA by 2026-03-15 to meet internal budget cycle.

Open questions / risks:
- How to define "sustained tokens/sec" for SLA (1-min vs 5-min window).
- Billing model for burst consumption (flat rate vs per-token premium).
- Impact of model switching/fallback on perceived latency and quality during bursts.
- Possibility of multi-tenant noisy neighbors in shared fallback pools — customer wants isolation guarantees when fallback invoked.

Stubs / refs: SOW draft in drive (sow-draft-v3.docx), POC performance report attached. Jira tickets INFRA-4127 (capacity ask) and SEC-2219 (SAML integration).

CRM shorthand / last touch: "Customer wants firm SLAs. Will sign if we can meet 40k+ sustainable tokens with predictable burst pricing. Legal cares about credit cap; finance needs price modeling by 3/15."
